title: CPU
text: Build a CPU that runs programs. Each instruction is a 16-bit word: its top four bits are the opcode and its low eight the operand n. It takes two clock cycles. In the first, the word on instr is kept and PC goes up by one; in the second, the instruction is carried out. The opcodes: 0 NOP: nothing; 1 LDI n: A = n; 2 LDA n: A = RAM[n]; 3 STA n: RAM[n] = A; 4 ADD n: A = A + RAM[n]; 5 SUB n: A = A - RAM[n]; 6 ADI n: A = A + n; 7 SBI n: A = A - n; 8 JMP n: PC = n; 9 JZ n: PC = n if Z; A JC n: PC = n if C; B OUT: out = A; C HLT: halt. D to F do nothing. Loads, additions and subtractions set Z when A becomes 0. Additions set C on a carry; subtractions set C when nothing is borrowed. pc is the address of the next word. For RAM[n], put n on addr: the byte there arrives on din. To store, hold A on dout and we at 1 through the second cycle. fetch is 1 during a first cycle. Once halted, halt is 1 and nothing changes. Registers, a multiplexer and an 8-bit adder are provided, and a ROM can decode the opcode. The main sheet is a computer to run your CPU in.
